evidence_items.publisher: Pan et al., arXiv; accepted at ICML 2026
evidence_items.explanation: The study collected deployment evidence from April through November 2025. It documents practical approaches to reliability, but does not independently establish sustained agent performance and separately measure the relevant commonsense competence.

The evaluation identifies failures relevant to Marcus's account of commonsense competence. Its simulated e-commerce tasks neither establish reliable real-world deployment nor show that such competence is universally necessary.

This is evidence of improvement in actual deployment. A relative improvement does not establish an absolute reliability standard, and the reported result does not test whether the agent lacks relevant commonsense competence.

The claim supplies no threshold that resolves whether constrained, supervised deployments count as reliable agents.
